articles.title: India Just Raised Cancer Drug Prices by 50 Per Cent. The Iran War Is in Every Chemo Ward Now.
articles.excerpt: Platinum shortages caused by the Gulf conflict have dried up supplies of cisplatin and carboplatin — the first-line drugs for lung, ovarian and bladder cancers. The price hike may restart production, but not everyone will be able to afford it.
articles.image_caption: A nurse prepares chemotherapy drugs for administration at a hospital
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with elderly parents or family members undergoing cancer treatment in India face higher costs and persistent drug shortages at government hospitals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Leaves for Europe Tomorrow With the Longest Agenda an Indian PM Has Carried to a G7.
articles.excerpt: Five days, two countries, one historic first and a fraught bilateral with Trump. From dead Indian sailors to H-1B visas to a trade deal deadline, here is everything on the table.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who departs for France on June 13
articles.nri_angle: The Modi-Trump bilateral will directly address H-1B visa policy, trade tariffs on Indian goods, and energy cooperation — all issues that shape daily life for NRIs in the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Leaked Iran Deal Gives Tehran Almost Everything It Wanted. India's Oil Bill Depends on What Happens Next.
articles.excerpt: A 14-point memorandum published by Iranian state media includes Hormuz reopening under Iranian control, $300 billion in reparations talks, and a 60-day nuclear deferral. Trump says the leak is fake. Oil has crashed to a two-month low.
articles.image_caption: The Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil shipments normally pass (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: A deal that reopens the Strait of Hormuz would ease oil prices, strengthen the rupee, and slow the inflation that has pushed up the cost of flights, remittances and household budgets in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foreign Investors Have Pulled $30 Billion From India This Year. BlackRock Says the Selling Has Gone Too Far.
articles.excerpt: India has lost more foreign investment in six months than in any full year on record. The world's largest asset manager says the AI panic and oil fear have masked the real story.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, where foreign investors have pulled a record 0 billion from Indian equities this year (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors with Indian equity exposure face the core question: have markets bottomed after a record $30 billion outflow, or is more pain ahead? BlackRock's contrarian call and the RBI's NRI deposit sweeteners could shape the answer.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS Just Partnered with the AI Company That Wiped $63 Billion Off India's IT Sector. It Plans to Give 50,000 Workers Access to Claude.
articles.excerpt: The partnership comes after Anthropic's tools triggered a $62.8 billion market-cap wipeout in Indian IT. TCS's chairman says the company is moving towards equal numbers of AI agents and human employees.
articles.image_caption: N. Chandrasekaran, chairman of Tata Sons and TCS, at a corporate event
articles.nri_angle: Hundreds of thousands of NRI tech workers on H-1B visas at IT services firms face job uncertainty as their employers deploy AI agents to replace the very roles that brought them to America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kevin Warsh Chairs His First Fed Meeting Next Week. India Has $30 Billion Worth of Reasons to Watch.
articles.excerpt: The new Fed chairman leads his first FOMC meeting on June 16 with US inflation at a three-year high, a possible Iran deal reshaping oil markets, and India's financial system hanging on every word.
articles.image_caption: Kevin Warsh, the new Federal Reserve chairman, who chairs his first FOMC meeting next week (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs face a direct trade-off between US and Indian deposit rates, while the Fed's decision on rates will affect everything from mortgage costs and tech-sector hiring in America to the rupee and foreign outflows from India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Inflation Just Hit a New-Series High. The Iran War Is Now in Every Grocery Bill.
articles.excerpt: Retail CPI rose to 3.93 percent in May after four fuel hikes. The RBI has raised its full-year forecast. Economists say 6 percent by December is no longer a tail risk.
articles.image_caption: A market in India — food prices are surging as the Iran war disrupts supply chains (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Rising Indian inflation erodes the purchasing power of remittances — the rupee at 95 per dollar means money sent home buys less in real terms, while RBI rate hikes would slow the economy the diaspora invests in.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Federal Judge Just Killed Trump's $100,000 H-1B Fee. Indians, Who Get 75% of All Approvals, Have the Most to Gain.
articles.excerpt: The Boston ruling calls it an unconstitutional tax. The White House says it will appeal. A Republican lawmaker wants Congress to impose the fee itself.
articles.image_caption: The John Joseph Moakley United States Courthouse in Boston where the H-1B fee ruling was issued
articles.nri_angle: Indians receive over 70% of all H-1B approvals — the $100K fee had priced thousands of Indian professionals and their employers out of the programme, and its removal is the biggest immigration relief for the diaspora in months.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Summoned America's Top Diplomat for the Second Time in Three Days. The Relationship Has Not Been This Strained in Years.
articles.excerpt: Two diplomatic protests in 72 hours over attacks on Indian-crewed ships mark the sharpest public rebuke New Delhi has delivered to Washington in the modern partnership.
articles.image_caption: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar whose ministry summoned the US deputy chief of mission in New Delhi twice in three days
articles.nri_angle: The India-US strategic partnership underpins visa programmes, defence deals, and tech investment flows that directly shape the lives of four million Indian Americans — a diplomatic crisis of this magnitude puts the broader bilateral agenda at risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Puts All Maritime Agencies on 'Heightened Alert' After Three Tanker Strikes in Five Days
articles.excerpt: The shipping ministry directive comes as trade unions demand answers, 300,000 Indian seafarers work on vessels worldwide, and New Delhi summons the US diplomat for a second time in three days
articles.image_caption: INS Vikrant, India's first domestically built aircraft carrier — the country has placed all maritime agencies on heightened alert (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: India supplies the largest merchant marine workforce in the world — over 300,000 seafarers — and many NRI families have relatives working on commercial vessels in the volatile Gulf region.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Claims a Secret Oil Mission Moved 100 Million Barrels Through Hormuz. His Energy Secretary Says He Knows Nothing.
articles.excerpt: The contradiction between the president and his own cabinet underscores the opacity of the Strait of Hormuz situation — and India, which imports 85% of its crude, needs clarity more than anyone
articles.image_caption: US President Donald Trump at the White House
articles.nri_angle: India imports 85% of its crude oil and was the destination for a large share of Hormuz throughput — the truth about what is actually getting through the Strait directly determines Indian energy bills and inflation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: EY, Deloitte and a Space Startup All Opened AI Centres in Bengaluru This Week. The Pattern Is Clear.
articles.excerpt: Three separate investments in one city in five days signal that India's tech capital is becoming the world's AI back office — with implications for every Indian technologist abroad
articles.image_caption: Bengaluru, India's technology capital, where EY, Deloitte and a space startup all opened AI centres this week (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Bengaluru's AI hiring boom is creating high-paying roles in AI engineering, digital twins, and immersive design that could accelerate the reverse brain drain — giving NRI technologists in the US and UK a reason to consider moving back.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Dead Sailors Have Put Modi in a Corner. He Meets Trump at the G7 Next Week.
articles.excerpt: Three seafarers killed, three ships struck in one week. Unions want answers. The opposition smells blood. And the G7 summit is days away.
articles.image_caption: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi faces domestic pressure over seafarer deaths ahead of a G7 meeting with Trump
articles.nri_angle: India has 300,000+ merchant sailors globally — many Indian-American families have relatives on Gulf shipping routes caught in the US-Iran blockade.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sensex Surges 1.2%, Rupee Set to Rally as Oil Crashes to Two-Month Lows on Iran Deal Hopes
articles.excerpt: All sixteen sectors in the green, Brent at $88.55, but Tehran says it has not signed anything yet — and IT stocks keep falling.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai — the Sensex surged over 1.2% on Friday as oil prices crashed (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: A weaker rupee boosts NRI remittance purchasing power but signals economic stress — a genuine Iran deal would stabilise the currency that shapes how far diaspora money stretches back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Waived Seven Years of Nuclear Import Duties. The Iran War Made It Urgent.
articles.excerpt: A finance ministry order retroactively clears customs on reactor equipment back to 2019 and extends duty-free status through 2035, signalling that energy independence has become a national security priority.
articles.image_caption: The Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant in Tamil Nadu — India has waived seven years of nuclear import duties (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI engineers have been central to India's nuclear programme, and the country's energy mix directly affects cost of living and economic growth back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Says Iran Deal Is 'All Wrapped Up.' India Is Not Celebrating Yet.
articles.excerpt: The US president says a signing could come this weekend and the Strait of Hormuz will reopen. Oil has already crashed below $87. But Tehran says it has not agreed to anything.
articles.image_caption: US President Donald Trump at the White House
articles.nri_angle: A deal reopening the Strait of Hormuz would crash oil prices, strengthen the rupee, ease inflation for NRIs in the Gulf, and reduce the risk to 300,000 Indian seafarers working in global shipping.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: USCIS Just Made It Harder to Get a Green Card Without Leaving the US. Indians Have the Most to Lose.
articles.excerpt: A new memo reframes adjustment of status as 'extraordinary relief' and pushes applicants toward consular processing abroad — a move that could add years to the wait for over a million Indians.
articles.image_caption: A US permanent resident card — a new USCIS memo threatens the green card path for over a million Indian nationals (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Over 1.1 million Indian nationals in the US employment-based green card backlog face longer waits, family separation, and job instability if adjustment of status becomes functionally unavailable.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The ECB Just Raised Rates for the First Time in Three Years. The Iran War Has Made Inflation Everyone's Problem.
articles.excerpt: The European Central Bank hiked to 2.25% as eurozone inflation hit 3.2%. Indian banks are offering NRIs up to 7% on deposits. The Fed decides next week.
articles.image_caption: ECB President Christine Lagarde — the European Central Bank raised rates to 2.25%, the first hike in nearly three years (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs in Europe face higher mortgage costs, but can lock in 5.75-7.1% on Indian bank deposits — and the weakening rupee makes remittances more valuable.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SpaceX Just Became a $1.77 Trillion Company. India Won't Let It Turn On Starlink.
articles.excerpt: The biggest IPO in history priced at $135 a share on Thursday. India froze Starlink's final clearance days before the debut.
articles.image_caption: SpaceX founder Elon Musk, whose company priced the largest IPO in history on Thursday
articles.nri_angle: SpaceX's public debut gives NRI investors access to the company behind Starlink, the satellite internet service that could transform rural connectivity in India — if regulators let it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Preparing to Let Its Fiscal Deficit Blow Past Target. The Iran War Left No Choice.
articles.excerpt: Authorities are willing to widen the gap to 4.8 per cent of GDP — half a percentage point above February's goal — as energy subsidies devour the budget.
articles.image_caption: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman during a meeting in Vienna in April 2025
articles.nri_angle: A wider fiscal deficit could weaken the rupee further, affect NRI deposit returns, and reshape the risk-reward calculus for diaspora investments in Indian bonds and equities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: He Filed 11 Fake H-1B Petitions, Forged Executive Signatures, and Became an American Citizen. Now the DOJ Wants It Back.
articles.excerpt: Indian-origin CEO Neeraj Sharma is among 17 naturalised citizens targeted in the Trump administration's expanding denaturalization campaign.
articles.image_caption: The Robert F. Kennedy Department of Justice Building in Washington, D.C.
articles.nri_angle: The accelerating denaturalization campaign is a wake-up call for the Indian-American community: citizenship obtained through fraud — even by employers, not employees — can have cascading consequences years later.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Noida International Airport Opens for Commercial Flights June 15, Giving Delhi-NCR a Second Gateway
articles.excerpt: India's largest greenfield airport at Jewar begins domestic operations with IndiGo, Akasa Air, and 140 weekly flights across 15 destinations
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the inauguration of Noida International Airport in Jewar, March 28, 2026
articles.image_credit: Government of India, GODL-India, via Wikimedia Commons
articles.nri_angle: NRIs flying into Delhi-NCR now have a second airport option that halves travel time to Agra and western UP, reshaping trip planning for diaspora visits home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nipah Virus Returns to Kerala: Kozhikode Case Confirmed as State Activates Outbreak Protocols
articles.excerpt: A 43-year-old man is on ventilator support as health authorities trace 77 contacts and deploy containment measures in a district that has battled the deadly virus repeatedly since 2018
articles.image_caption: Electron micrograph of Nipah virus particles from an infected VERO cell
articles.image_credit: CDC / C.S. Goldsmith, P.E. Rollin, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with summer travel plans to Kerala face renewed health concerns as Nipah — a WHO priority pathogen with 40-75% mortality — resurfaces in Kozhikode, the state's most popular diaspora gateway after Kochi.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Inflation Just Hit a Three-Year High. The Fed May Hike Rates. Here Is What That Means for India.
articles.excerpt: Consumer prices rose 4.2 per cent in May as the Iran oil shock ripples through the American economy. Producer prices surged even faster. For NRIs with mortgages, investments and families back home, the math just changed.
articles.image_caption: The Federal Reserve building in Washington, D.C.
articles.nri_angle: Rising US inflation and potential Fed rate hikes directly affect NRI mortgage costs, dollar-rupee remittance rates, and the trajectory of FPI flows into Indian markets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Tells the US It Does Not Have Overcapacity in Anything. Washington Disagrees.
articles.excerpt: As America's Section 301 probe targets 16 countries, India's top trade official fires back with a blunt defence: per capita consumption is too low for overcapacity to exist. A $42 billion trade surplus hangs in the balance.
articles.image_caption: India and the United States are locked in a trade dispute over alleged manufacturing overcapacity
articles.nri_angle: Section 301 tariffs on Indian goods would directly affect NRI-linked businesses in textiles, steel and IT services, and could disrupt the broader India-US trade deal that both sides are negotiating.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Meta and Reliance to Build India's First AI Data Centre in Jamnagar, Marking a New Chapter in the $13 Billion Race
articles.excerpt: The 168 MW facility in Gujarat deepens the Zuckerberg-Ambani alliance and positions India as a serious contender in the global AI infrastructure buildout
articles.image_caption: Mukesh Ambani, chairman of Reliance Industries, which will build and operate the facility
articles.nri_angle: India's first hyperscale AI data centre could improve Meta platform performance for 500M+ Indian users and NRIs, while creating high-skill tech jobs that make return migration more attractive.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Cancels Iran Strikes at the Last Minute. Oil Crashed. India Is Watching the Fine Print.
articles.excerpt: Brent crude dropped 3.7 per cent to $89 after Trump said a deal had been approved by Iran, Israel, Saudi Arabia and a dozen other nations. But the naval blockade stays — and India still imports 85 per cent of its oil.
articles.image_caption: Donald Trump announced the cancellation of strikes on Iran via Truth Social on Thursday evening
articles.nri_angle: Gulf-based Indian workers face direct safety risks, and any deal would ease India's $30B+ oil import pressure and stabilise remittances worth $32 billion annually.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Ebola Outbreak Just Got the Highest WHO Alarm. Here Is What Every NRI Travelling This Summer Needs to Know.
articles.excerpt: Suspected cases have topped 900 in Congo. The US has restricted green card holders from three African countries. And the World Cup has just begun.
articles.image_caption: Health workers in protective equipment respond to an Ebola outbreak — the WHO has issued its highest alarm level (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs face new US entry screening rules, green card holders from affected African countries risk temporary entry limits, and Indian diaspora workers across East Africa are in proximity to the spreading outbreak.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Refiners Have Quietly Secured Oil Through August. Here Is How They Did It.
articles.excerpt: Ship-to-ship transfers off Fujairah, spot cargoes from Brazil and West Africa, and 4 million barrels of UAE crude. India's supply chain is holding — but the price is steep.
articles.image_caption: Jamnagar Refinery, the world's largest oil refining complex — Indian refiners have quietly locked in crude supply through August (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with rupee investments, Indian property or remittance flows are directly affected — sustained high oil prices weaken the rupee, inflate costs, and erode the dollar value of Indian assets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Wants to Seize Iran's Oil Hub. India Buys 85 Per Cent of Its Crude From Abroad.
articles.excerpt: The US president threatened to take Kharg Island, through which 90 per cent of Iranian oil exports flow. Brent is at $93. India's import bill is already at record levels.
articles.image_caption: Oil refinery (Pexels)
articles.nri_angle: India imports 85% of its crude oil and the Iran war has pushed Brent to $93, weakened the rupee 6% to 95.76, and triggered record FPI outflows — a Kharg Island seizure could push oil past $100.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The World Bank Just Called India the Fastest-Growing Major Economy. It Called the Rest of the Decade a Write-Off.
articles.excerpt: Global growth slashed to 2.5 per cent — and could crash to 1.3 per cent if the Iran war deepens. Oil at $94 a barrel is already rewriting the math for every NRI sending money home.
articles.image_caption: Global economic indicators on a trading screen
articles.nri_angle: India's 6.6% growth and the rupee at 95.76 mean NRI remittances and investments buy more, but $94 oil and a potential lost decade for developing nations threaten the long-term outlook.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Indian-American Is Running the Biggest Security Operation in American History. The World Cup Just Kicked Off.
articles.excerpt: FBI Director Kash Patel called the tournament 'the biggest lift in FBI history.' He has 300,000 background checks, 46 foreign police forces, and Iran's cyber-warfare team to worry about.
articles.image_caption: FBI Director Kash Patel, the first Indian-American to lead the bureau
articles.nri_angle: Kash Patel, the son of Gujarati immigrants from East Africa, is the first Indian-American FBI director and now leads the largest security operation in US history.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The World Cup Has Started. Here Is What Every Indian Fan Needs to Know.
articles.excerpt: Forty-eight teams, three host nations, and Indian fans glued to screens at 12:30 AM. The biggest FIFA World Cup in history kicks off with Mexico versus South Africa in Mexico City.
articles.image_caption: Estadio Azteca in Mexico City, host venue for the FIFA World Cup 2026 opening match
articles.nri_angle: NRIs in US and Canadian host cities can attend matches in their backyards. Indian fans watching from India face late-night kickoffs on new Zee5/Unite8 platform. Kash Patel, the Indian-American FBI director, is leading the largest security operation in US history for the tournament.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Indian Sailors Are Dead. India Says the US Navy Has Struck Three Ships With Indian Crews This Week.
articles.excerpt: India summoned the American chargé d'affaires and demanded the attacks stop. The US blockade of Iranian oil has now killed its first civilians — all three were Indian.
articles.image_caption: Satellite view of the Strait of Hormuz, where the US blockade has targeted ships carrying Indian crews
articles.nri_angle: India has 300,000+ sailors in global shipping fleets. Three were killed by US strikes enforcing the Iran blockade — the first civilian deaths. India summoned the US diplomat and demanded attacks stop. Raises questions about Indian seafarer safety in militarised shipping lanes and deepens US-India diplomatic strain at a critical moment.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Opendoor Just Shut Its India Operations. Its Stock Jumped 8 Percent.
articles.excerpt: The home-buying platform says AI-native teams in the US can do what 250 workers in India used to do. Investors and outsourcing analysts say it is the beginning of a much larger shift.
articles.image_caption: A technology office building in India, the hub of the outsourcing industry
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's IT Stocks Have Fallen for Seven Straight Sessions. They Have Lost Over 10 Percent.
articles.excerpt: Anthropic's new tools, Opendoor's India exit, and US inflation at a three-year high are hammering the sector that built modern India's middle class.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, where India's IT sector is in a seven-session losing streak
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Trillion-Dollar Companies Are About to Hit Wall Street. All Three Are AI.

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Fertiliser Bill Has Doubled in Three Months. The Iran War Is Draining the Treasury.

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: No Indian PM Has Visited Slovakia in 33 Years. Modi Is About to Change That.

articles.title: India Just Became Europe's Official AI Partner. The Pitch Starts in Nice.
articles.excerpt: VivaTech 2026 has named India its Official AI Partner Country. IIT Madras is bringing hyperloop tech and indigenous 6G to France. Modi will seal it.

articles.title: India Summoned the American Envoy. The US Just Struck a Ship With 24 Indians on Board.
articles.excerpt: New Delhi handed Washington a formal protest after a US aircraft fired on the tanker Settebello off Oman, leaving three Indian seafarers missing. The diplomatic fallout comes days before Modi and Trump are expected to meet at the G7.
articles.image_caption: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, who summoned the US envoy after a strike on a ship carrying Indian nationals (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: India's 8 million citizens in Gulf states face growing risks from the Iran-US conflict. The diplomatic standoff over civilian shipping adds a new layer of tension to the India-US relationship that directly affects diaspora safety and the upcoming Modi-Trump G7 bilateral.

articles.title: Scientists Say a 'Godzilla' El Niño Is Building in the Pacific. India May Be Its Biggest Casualty.
articles.excerpt: Three-quarters of climate models now predict the developing El Niño could reach 2.5°C of warming — rivalling the strongest event ever recorded. For India, the stakes are existential: a weakened monsoon, surging food prices, and a power grid already running at record demand.
articles.image_caption: Sea surface temperature anomaly map showing El Niño conditions in the Pacific — a strong event could disrupt India's monsoon season (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs sending remittances to families in agricultural regions face the prospect of crop failures and food inflation. Rising food and power costs will hit middle-class households across India, while diaspora investors watch the rupee and Indian equities take a double hit from oil and climate risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran Has Declared the Strait of Hormuz Closed. India Just Lost Its Most Important Oil Route.
articles.excerpt: The first full closure of the world's most critical energy chokepoint since the 1980s threatens to push Brent crude past $100, hammers Indian markets, and puts 8 million Gulf-based Indians in an increasingly volatile region.
articles.image_caption: Commercial vessels transit the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway through which one-fifth of global oil shipments normally pass
articles.nri_angle: Eight million Indians in Gulf states face growing instability; oil price surge hits rupee, inflation, and Indian markets; India summoned US diplomat over tanker strike on Indian sailors.

articles.title: Indians Have Founded 96 of America's Billion-Dollar Startups. No Other Immigrant Group Comes Close.
articles.excerpt: A new study from the National Foundation for American Policy finds immigrants built 59 per cent of all US unicorns — with Indian-origin founders leading the pack by a massive margin, even as the MAGA movement targets them.
articles.image_caption: Silicon Valley, where Indian-origin entrepreneurs have founded more billion-dollar startups than any other immigrant group
articles.nri_angle: Indian immigrants founded 96 US unicorn startups, more than any other group; median Indian household income $150K; data directly counters anti-Indian MAGA narrative amid H-1B fee fights and EB-2 retrogression.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Has Frozen Starlink's Final Clearance. The Iran War Made the Decision.
articles.excerpt: Security agencies under the Home Ministry have withheld approvals after Starlink terminals were reportedly used in Iran without a licence. The freeze also stalls satellite spectrum pricing for all providers.
articles.image_caption: Starlink satellite constellation operated by SpaceX
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Retail Investors Just Blinked. Equity Fund Inflows Crashed 40% in May.
articles.excerpt: The sharpest monthly drop in a year has arrived, and Bernstein warns that SIP investors — the market's last line of defence — may not wait much longer for returns that have stopped coming.

articles.excerpt: A Reuters poll of 38 economists forecasts India's CPI inflation at 4% in May — breaching the Reserve Bank's target for the first time since early 2025 — as fuel price hikes and vegetable costs tear through household budgets.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Federal Court Strikes Down Trump's $100K H-1B Fee as GOP Lawmaker Moves to Codify It
articles.excerpt: A Boston judge rules the fee was an unauthorized tax, but the PROTECT Act could revive it through Congress — leaving Indian tech workers in limbo
